reachable:
A batcher can only act through the trained weights — it is not called at scoring time, and there is nothing to reach at the scored position. The right reachability question is whether it changes the training distribution at all, and it does, substantially and in the direction claimed: measured batch depth mix .09/.14/.23/.55 versus uniform .29/.30/.21/.19, and 46.3 same-(image, normalized-read-path, depth) pairs per batch versus 6.8 under uniform sampling (run3.py). Every batch member contributes loss at all of its command rows, so the reweighting gets gradient by construction.

The stratification variable is well aligned with the scored skill, which I checked because the author flagged mis-labeling as failure mode #5. It is not mis-labeled: the depth-3 stratum is 534/547 pure-mv chains and the depth-4 stratum is 508/508 pure-mv, and for essentially every sequence at depth >= 2 the deepest routed read carries meta arm=cups, role=cups_test. The cvar `cat A > B` / `cat A >> B` extension the author kept from the parent contributes almost entirely at depth 1 (317 of 737) and does not contaminate the deep strata (roles.py cross-tab: labeled depth vs mv-only depth is diagonal at d=1,4 and 534/547 diagonal at d=3).

The in-batch-negative half is also live rather than inert: the genome's objective r22_exact_target_equivalence_quotient builds a full pairwise equivalence/ring/repulsion structure over all command rows in the batch, so the collision blocks feed it directly. The author's failure clause #4 does not fire.

Contract compliance verified by execution: exactly 64 in-bounds indices per call over 4000 steps; identical batch stream under different global torch seeds (deterministic, private generators only); the global torch RNG is bit-identical before and after 49 steps; fit is unmutated. Cost is comparable to the parent as claimed — setup 0.077s vs the parent's 0.045s, 0.231 ms/step vs 0.166 ms/step, negligible against training.
solves_outside_model:
No. The module resolves the move/copy chain in Python and computes exact hop counts, but the only thing that leaves make_batcher is a list of integer indices, which _train uses solely to index fit_stripped before stream.collate. Nothing resolved is written into a token, a target, or any scoring-time tensor; nothing is written back into the fit dicts (verified: z_cmd checksums unchanged after a run). The batcher is not invoked at scoring time at all, so the withheld observation at the read cannot switch any part of it on or off. The stream axis is unchanged (baseline_interleave), so the read-token-parity invariant is untouched.

The one thing worth naming explicitly: _refine_block reads z_obs — the read's ANSWER embedding — at setup, to decide which sequences co-occur in a batch. That is answer information used for SAMPLE SELECTION on the train split, which is the permitted side of the line, and it is doubly moot here because the filter never removes anything. This is not the retracted r-prior shape.
summary:
The mechanism is implemented exactly as specified and the genome claim "axis: batcher; no other axis changed" is true — objective/arch/optim/target/stream/head are identical to the parent r4-07-complement-address-transport in the archive. The exact-integer-quota core works precisely as advertised: the largest-remainder allocation is realized to three decimals (measured late-half batch mix .090/.139/.225/.546 against the .089/.138/.225/.548 predicted from the real stratum sizes), the depth label is a faithful proxy for mv-chain depth on the scored skill, the collision blocks produce a 6.8x increase in in-batch same-read-path pairs, and the objective this genome carries actually consumes in-batch negatives. Contract compliance, determinism, RNG hygiene, non-mutation and cost all check out by execution, and the author correctly labeled the whole write-up UNMEASURED (the one hard number, n=89 / d3 60 / d4+ 29, came from the BRIEF, not fabricated).

What does not survive contact with the data is the argument for why it should matter. The hypothesis is built on the premise that deep chains are a small minority of training material; on the real split there is no depth-0 stratum at all and 41% of sequences already sit at depth 3-4. The realized effect is a 2.54x visit amplification for depth-4 and 1.07x for depth-3, with depth-1/2 pushed down to 0.39x/0.55x — a moderate reweighting, not the order-of-magnitude reallocation the write-up argues for, and the author's own jail sample (12 of 24 sequences at depth 3+) already contradicted the inference. Two named sub-mechanisms are provably inert on this root: the max_repeat cap and min_stratum floor can never bind (caps compute to 64 while quotas are bounded by 48), and the projection filter kept from the crossover partner removed zero members from 399 buckets because the property it tests already holds everywhere. The "epoch reshuffle without replacement" headline governs 24% of slots; 51% come from the block path and 26% from uniform fill.

Nothing here is a shortcut and nothing reaches the model's input. The candidate is scoreable; the archive description should be read with the magnitude claims and the two inert knobs caveated.

divergences.claim: The motivating premise: "a model trained mostly on 0- and 1-hop material has almost no gradient signal for composing 3 and 4 hops... If deep chains are a small minority of the training split (which the depth structure of this data suggests)", and the worked example n=6000 with |S_0..S_4| = 1800/2400/1200/480/120 where depth-4 is amplified ~9x and "42% of every batch after the ramp carries a depth-3-or-deeper chain".
divergences.what_the_code_does: Run on the real training split with the candidate's own labeler, there is NO depth-0 stratum at all and the split is already depth-rich. Full train.jsonl: n=2560, strata d0..d4 = 0/737/768/547/508 (41% of sequences at depth 3+). After split_train_dev(seed=0): n=2304, 0/672/693/491/448. Realized per-sequence visit amplification over 4000 steps at bs=64 is 2.54x for depth-4 and 1.07x for depth-3, with depth-1 and depth-2 DOWN-weighted to 0.39x and 0.55x. The batch depth mix (late half) is .09/.14/.23/.55 versus uniform .29/.30/.21/.19. The reallocation is real but it is a ~2.5x tilt on already-abundant deep material, not the order-of-magnitude rescue the hypothesis argues for. This is the author's own failure clause #2, and it was checkable in the jail: the 24 sequences of evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl give depths {1:3, 2:9, 3:4, 4:8} — 50% depth-3+ — under the candidate's own _deepest_routed_read.
divergences.evidence: scratchpad/s8/strata.py (full split), run2.py (fit split + 4000-step realized composition and per-sequence visit counts), and the jail-sample count above. Predicted quota at r=1 from the real fit sizes is d1..d4 = 1/4/11/32 of 48 stratified slots; the measured late-half mix .090/.139/.225/.546 matches the predicted .089/.138/.225/.548 to three decimals.

divergences.claim: "Each stratum quota is clamped by caps[d] = min(|S_d|, bs, max_repeat*bs*|S_d|/n), which bounds how many times a sequence in that stratum is visited... the caps hold that below the 20x ceiling", and "The base_frac=0.25 uniform reserve and the max_repeat=20 cap are the two knobs that bound this."
divergences.what_the_code_does: On this data the cap is provably inert. Every stratum has size >= 448 >> min_stratum=16, and room = 20*64*size/n >= 20*64*448/2304 = 248, so caps = [0, 64, 64, 64, 64] while the largest-remainder allocation can never assign more than n_str = bs - round(0.25*bs) = 48 to any stratum. The clamp branch and the surplus-redistribution loop are therefore dead code for this root, and min_stratum never excludes anything. Only base_frac is a live bound. Not a correctness bug — the code is as written — but the guard the hypothesis and the module DESCRIPTION advertise does not guard here.
divergences.evidence: sizes from run2.py; caps arithmetic from the impl lines 246-252 with n=2304, bs=64, max_repeat=20; counts[d] <= n_str = 48 by construction at impl lines 259-272.

divergences.claim: "I kept from the partner: the 'same query, different answer' test in embedding space... a block is a set of sequences that the symbolic key says share a read shape AND the projection says agree on the read command while disagreeing on the read answer", and "the collision blocks additionally guarantee that... their answers are verified distinct in projection."
divergences.what_the_code_does: _refine_block never removes a single member on real embeddings: 399 buckets entered with 2256 members and 2256 came out, zero buckets shrunk. Measured on the standardized cache, the minimum command similarity to member 0 under the fixed projection is 0.67 (threshold sim_thresh=0.6, 0% below) and the maximum answer-pair similarity is 0.978 (threshold ans_max_sim=0.995, 0% above). The property already holds for every symbolic bucket, so the crossover half kept from the partner selects nothing — it is a paid no-op. Separately, the filter fails OPEN rather than closed: when fewer than two members survive it returns the unfiltered `rows` (impl lines 146-148), and it returns `members` untouched if any member lacks z_cmd/z_obs, so the word "guarantee" is not enforced even in principle.
divergences.evidence: scratchpad/s8/run2.py — instrumented wrapper around _refine_block over the real emb-seq-train.pt after standardization: {'in': 2256, 'out': 2256, 'buckets': 399}, no 'shrunk'; qsim min/med/max 0.67/0.962/1.0, answer-pair sim med/max 0.368/0.978.

divergences.claim: "replaces with-replacement drawing with random reshuffling inside each stratum... Inside a stratum the draw is therefore WITHOUT replacement until the whole stratum has been seen... Random reshuffling is the standard variance-reduced alternative to i.i.d. SGD sampling."
divergences.what_the_code_does: Over a full 4000-step run only 24.0% of the 256,000 slots come from the epoch cursor. 51.0% come from the block path, which bypasses the cursor entirely and draws with torch.multinomial weighted by 1 + routed-read-count, and 25.6% come from the plain uniform randint fill. The claimed variance reduction is therefore largely not realized: depth-4 sequences receive 86 to 368 visits (mean 282) rather than the near-constant count strict reshuffling would give. The disclosure is present as item 5 of the spec (blocks fire with probability block_frac_max*r = 0.5 after the ramp), so this is an overstated headline rather than a contradiction. Cursor pulls discarded by the in-batch dedup are negligible (776 of 62,273, 1.2%).
divergences.evidence: scratchpad/s8/run4.py (counter-instrumented copy of the impl): block 130503 (0.51), cursor 61497 (0.24), unif 65604 (0.256), pulldrop 776 of 62273 pull requests; run2.py per-depth visit min/mean/max.

divergences.claim: "Both parents draw with replacement everywhere (torch.randint, torch.multinomial(replacement=True))".
divergences.what_the_code_does: The parent r2_routed_collision_depth_batcher picks block members with torch.multinomial(member_w[bi], k, replacement=False, generator=g) at line 163. Bucket selection and the uniform fill are with replacement, so the thrust is right, but the parenthetical is wrong about the parent's source.
